newsitem.title: SOUTH AFRICA: Strike ends at Engen refinery - radio.
newsitem.headline: Strike ends at Engen refinery - radio.

text.p: South African radio said that workers on strike since Monday at Engen's Durban refinery would return to work on Friday.
General manager Peter Dent said earlier on Thursday that the strike by some 120 out of 520 workers had not affected production as the refinery was already down for maintenance.
"The week-long deadlock between the Chemical Workers' Industrial Union and management of the Engen refinery in Durban has been broken," the radio said.
"The union and management agreed after today's talks that both parties had negotiated in good faith."
The workers, who began their strike on Monday afternoon, were demanding that written warnings issued last Tuesday for a two-hour work stoppage in support of the union be withdrawn.

"The strike has not affected production at all because we were down for maintenance any way. The supply situation is unaffected because we have plenty in tankage and also recently received imports," Dent said.
The strike was restricted to workers from the operating areas of the plant, he said.
